I give up. I did not modify `/work/putnam_2022_b6.lean`, so it still contains the original `sorry`.

The statement is the full classification from Putnam 2022 B6: every continuous solution is f(x) = 1/(1+cx) with c ≥ 0. The reverse direction is routine algebra. For f(x) = 1/(1+cx), both sides of the equation reduce to 1 + 1/(1+c(x+y)), since f(x f(y)) = (1+cy)/(1+cx+cy) and f(y f(x)) = (1+cx)/(1+cx+cy). The forward direction is the hard part: showing that every continuous solution has this form. I don't have a reliable argument for that step, and writing it in Lean would require many supporting lemmas that I haven't worked out. A partial proof would not satisfy the rules, so I'm stopping here.
